summary.headline: Gateway Distriparks Q1 FY27: ICD volumes stagnant YoY on West Asia war disruption; management still targets double-digit FY27 growth; no financial figures disclosed on call.
summary.overview: Management said ICD market has de-grown in its operating markets since April due to the West Asia conflict, but Gateway's market share is intact. Volumes were flat YoY, with June and July trends similar to Q1 and July hit by weather-related port and double-stacking restrictions. Rail EBITDA per TEU was lower on weaker imports, lower double stacking, higher empty running and fuel and minimum wage costs, with pass-through expected to show in Q2. Snowman Logistics reported 5-7% warehousing price increases and guided 10-15% top-line growth, with about 24,000 additional pallets by end FY27. The call did not disclose quarterly financial figures in the transcript.

segments.name: ICD / Rail (Gateway Distriparks)
segments.commentary: Volumes stagnant YoY; market share intact; rail EBITDA per TEU lower on import-export mix, weaker double stacking (39%), higher underframe and empty running. Domestic business about 500 containers per month.

segments.name: CFS (Gateway Distriparks)
segments.commentary: Management says volume improvements and a pricing increase after fuel and wage hikes could lift margins, possibly visible in Q2. A land-sale exercise about 1.5 years ago failed on valuation; no active sale process.

segments.name: Snowman Logistics
segments.commentary: Warehousing pricing up 5%-7%; 5PL service margin 5%-6%; Pune pallet capacity due in a couple of months, Patna next, about 24,000 additional pallets by end FY27; no new 5PL customers in Q1, possibly by Q3/Q4.

guidance_outlook: Gateway: management hopes to close FY27 with double-digit volume growth, conditional on West Asia conflict easing.
Medium term: double-digit growth 'easy to achieve' once the war situation clears; new ICDs to add to growth.
Snowman: 10%-15% top-line growth guided for this year and next, across all segments.
Rail EBITDA: expected to recover to the older range as volumes return; fuel and wage cost impact more visible in Q2.
Tax: cash tax expected at about 18.88% for 7-8 years, using accumulated MAT credit.
capex_capacity: Indore ICD: about 26.4 acres after 2.5 acres added; construction slowed by rains, full swing after September; operational by 2028.

Ankleshwar ICD: initial customs permission received; EXIM operations expected to start by end-September 2026 (Q2). Existing ICD there handles about 5,000 TEU (estimate); management expects Ankleshwar to reach a similar level in 3-4 years.
Jaipur ICD: legal matter listed for final arguments in September; no resolution yet.
Snowman: Pune pallet expansion due in a couple of months, Patna next; about 24,000 pallets added by end of this year.
Land bank about 475 acres across India, mostly freehold; Garhi land (85-90 acres) indicated at INR25-30 crore per acre for outright purchase.
demand_pricing: ICD market de-grew in Gateway's markets since April on West Asia war; imports dried up in April-May and improved from June-July.
July volumes hit by weather, port congestion and double-stacking restrictions at Mundra, Pipavav and JNPT.
DFC last connection to JNPT completed; management says cargo shift to JNPT will take a couple of months to be visible; shipping lines may prefer single-dip, about 1-2% annual road-to-rail shift.
JNPT rail haulage about 6 slabs higher than Mundra, making it costlier for North India at current pricing; possible special haulage relief is unconfirmed industry talk.
CONCOR cited as largest competitor in India.

qa_highlights.question: Is the flat ICD volume a market-share loss, and what is the outlook for the rest of FY27?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said market share is intact and the market has de-grown; it still expects double-digit growth for the year, with the medium-term path dependent on the war ending.

qa_highlights.question: Why is rail EBITDA per TEU declining while market share holds?
qa_highlights.answer: Lower imports, higher exports, lower double stacking, higher underframe and empty running reduced margins; fuel and Haryana minimum wage hikes (35%) add cost, with pass-through lagging into Q2.

qa_highlights.question: What is the CFS business's future and land-sale option?
qa_highlights.answer: A sale exercise about 1.5 years ago failed on valuation; no active process since net debt reached about zero. Pricing increase may improve margin in Q2.

qa_highlights.question: Will Ankleshwar and JNPT change volumes and economics?
qa_highlights.answer: Ankleshwar EXIM starts by end-September; JNPT is about 5% of rail. Management said JNPT revenue and EBITDA per TEU would be higher on current pricing given distance, but North customers face higher inland cost.

qa_highlights.question: What are contingent liabilities of INR6,000 crore?
qa_highlights.answer: About 95% are bonds to government authorities, mainly customs, linked to bonded cargo; not expected claims.

qa_highlights.question: What pricing and capacity are planned for Snowman?
qa_highlights.answer: Average 5%-7% pricing increase achieved; further revisions depend on renewals; about 24,000 pallets added this year.

risks_watch: West Asia conflict prolonging import weakness and ICD volume stagnation.
Rail margin pressure from low double stacking, empty running and higher fuel and minimum wage costs; Q2 pass-through to be tested.
Ankleshwar EXIM start-up timing (end-September) and Indore (2028) and Jaipur litigation timelines.
Shipping line decisions on JNPT versus Gujarat ports; special haulage relief is unconfirmed.
Tax rate normalisation after MAT credit use over 7-8 years.
summary.management_tone: Confident on long-term growth and market share but cautious on the near term, repeatedly tying volume recovery to the West Asia conflict. Management was evasive on specific June-July volumes, JNPT haulage relief, and land valuation, citing listing restrictions or lack of data.

So right now, it's zero, EXIM has not started. It will only start by end of September.
Almost 95% of that amount are bonds given to government authorities, mainly customs.
We're looking at growth of, say, 10% to 15% on top line and it will be across all the segments.
